issues.note: House rule: a subsense limited to one form states it in its explanation.
Split by grammar is allowed; boundary is blurred mainly by the misleading adaptation note.
Form restriction in explanation is house practice; possessive hint is useful, collocations show it.
Note says fire powder is uncountable, yet subsense a and examples use plural ashes.
Rightly notes the adaptation note implies only the body sense is plural.
Naming the form ashes is sanctioned in explanation; grammar value does not name it.
Entry headword is ash; ashes is a listed form, so no hand mark needed.
Known funeral formula, but a liturgical quotation rather than a frequent idiom.
Same contradiction: plural ashes of a fire versus note's uncountable fire powder.
Signpost has four words; house limit is one to three.
Fireplace ashes are remains of burned wood; fits loosely, though definition wording is narrow.
Rise is not the entry headword; the site marks ashes automatically.
Definitions do differ (remains of a destroyed thing); wording could sharpen the contrast.
Note misstates the trap: fire remains also commonly take plural ashes.

findings.F1: Entry-level grammar adaptation note says ash from a fire is uncountable and only a person's remains are plural, contradicting subsense 1a and its plural examples and collocations.
findings.F2: Sense 2 signpost "of a dead person" has four words, over the three-word limit.
